title: The Hilbert-Samuel function of a finite module and of a finite-length quotient differ by a bounded amount
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For finite modules M' contained in M with finite length quotient, the lemma produces constants c_1 and c_2 such that the Hilbert-Samuel function of M at n is squeezed between c_1 plus that of M' at n minus c_2 and c_1 plus that of M' at n (statement lines 14261-14270). The proof does not estimate the two functions by polynomials: it takes c_1 to be the length of the quotient, splits the length of M modulo a power of I additively, compares the resulting terms by the containments available inside M', and uses I^{c_2}M contained in M' to shift the index for the other inequality (proof lines 14272-14302). The choice of c_2 and the index shift are the content, and both displayed chains of equalities are given. H2.
